plan.vision: A lightweight, cross-platform DOCX editor that allows users to create, edit, and save DOCX files without the need for heavy dependencies or external APIs. The project will focus on providing a minimalistic, yet functional, solution for basic document editing needs.

functions: add_heading(document: Document, text: str, level: int) -> Heading

plan.lessons_learned: This project avoids past mistakes by using memory-mapped files for efficient data handling, prioritizing algorithmic efficiency over OOP overhead, and ensuring that all dependencies are pinned in a virtual environment. The repository will be kept lightweight by excluding heavy directories with .gitignore, and clear setup scripts will be provided for reproducibility. There are no hidden paid-API dependencies.
plan.commit_message: Initial commit implementing a lightweight, cross-platform DOCX editor with basic document creation, editing, and saving functionality.

files_to_generate.instructions: Contains the main logic for loading, saving, and modifying DOCX documents. Use the `Document`, `Paragraph`, and `Heading` classes from `document.py`. Functions should include `load_document`, `save_document`, `add_paragraph`, and `add_heading`.

Defines the `Document`, `Paragraph`, and `Heading` classes. The `Document` class should manage a list of `Paragraph` and `Heading` objects. The `Paragraph` and `Heading` classes should store their respective text and, for `Heading`, the heading level.

Contains the unit test suite. Import and use the actual generated modules `docx_editor` and `document`. Tests should cover the creation, modification, and saving of documents, as well as the addition of paragraphs and headings. Ensure that the tests do not rely on complex mocks.
Provides an overview of the project, including the architecture, how to install and run the project, and any other relevant details. Include a Mermaid diagram for clarity.
Exclude venv, __pycache__, .env, and other heavy directories to keep the repository lightweight.
A setup script to install the necessary dependencies and create a virtual environment. Pin all dependencies to ensure consistency.
List all the required Python packages, keeping them lightweight and avoiding heavy ML libraries.
Include a standard open-source license, such as MIT, to clarify the terms of use and distribution.
